subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'll keep this a static model without joints, just a parts-based builder. I'm sketching the overall dimensions: an 11-meter-long hull, 3-meter width, with six wheels arranged across three axles at 0.65m radius.

Now I'm laying out the vehicle sections — chassis hull, front cab with a sloped windshield, deployed outrigger stabilizer legs touching the ground, and a railgun gantry mounted on top. I'm positioning the long rail barrels as parallel boxes with a gap between them, running the length of the hull with an overhang, plus coil rings along the barrel.

I'm computing the tilt angle for the rail assembly, defining a gun-axis direction vector and placing the barrel boxes along it with proper orientation, while adding cylindrical capacitor banks lying along the deck near the rear and figuring out the muzzle height at an 8° elevation.

I'm setting up a helper function to position parts along the gun's local axes, then planning the surface treatments: olive countershade camo paint, decal textures like hazard stripes and insignia stars, plane-geometry panels for cab windows and radar screens, and glow materials for coils and glass. Now I'm thinking through how to model the wheels, likely using a lathe or cylinder geometry.

Writing wheel and fender geometry...

Now I'm working out axle positions for the six wheels (three per side), spacing them along the z-axis under the hull and cab, then placing outrigger legs between the middle and rear wheel pairs.

Designing the outrigger leg assembly: a horizontal arm from the hull mount out to the cylinder position, a telescoping hydraulic cylinder going down, and an octagonal foot pad at the bottom, braced by a diagonal rod back to the hull — checking clearance against the wheel's outer radius.

Now I'm working out the cab geometry: a lower hood box, an upper cab box, and a sloped windshield built by extruding a side profile along the vehicle's width axis.

I'll add glass panels for the windshield and side windows with reflective texture, then plan out the cab's headlights, bumper, grille, and roof-mounted sensor mast, radar dish, antennas, and beacon, before laying out the main hull and armor plate dimensions.

Now I'm figuring out the upper hull deck height and adding fenders and skirts over the wheels, then working out the gun mount geometry -- trunnion pylons, breech housing, and the lateral rail positions in the gun's local coordinate frame.

Still computing gun geometry...

Positioning the ring sides and top/bottom bars around the rails with dark steel coloring and a cyan glow accent on the capacitor top bar, then moving to the rear breech housing as an armored plate box with cylindrical capacitor banks on the rear deck.

Placing eight capacitor cylinders at two z-depths with glowing end caps and cyan bands, then adding hydraulic elevation rods connecting the hull deck to the gun's underside, and finishing with a muzzle brake block with a glow slit plus a shroud near the barrel tip.

I also want heat sink fins on the side rails, merging geometry by color to keep part count manageable around 200 parts, and I'm planning a small texture set: star roundel insignia, hazard stripes, a warning label, glass, grille, and unit numbers.

For the armor paint, I'm designing a camo pattern using layered noise to blend olive tones with darker and lighter patches, plus a subtle countershading effect darker at the bottom and lighter on top.

I'm checking the SDK exports for noise, mix, and smoothstep, and pulling in a metal kit for steel and iron materials along with a panelled texture for hull plating with rivets. For the tires, I'm planning a dark base color with tread lugs arranged in a ring of twelve blocks around each wheel to simulate grip texture.

Now I'm working out a merge helper that combines all the tread lug boxes into one geometry per wheel using mergeGeometries, pulling in the BufferGeometryUtils import to keep part counts efficient. Writing wheel geometry math...

I'm placing the hubcap texture and checking tread lug heights so they don't dip the wheel below ground contact, adjusting lug center to .68 to stay within tolerance. Then I'm positioning the axle rod connecting the wheels and planning the differential housing.

Now I'm laying out the hull: a main panelled armor box, a dark underside skid plate, and deciding to skip a rear superstructure for now. I'm also considering adding side tool boxes or skirts between the wheel gaps near the leg mounts.

Then I work out stowage box placement between wheels, settling on a toolbox/fuel tank at z=-0.6 on both sides with specific dimensions, and start planning the leg geometry—mounting points on the hull sides and the horizontal arm extending outward.

Now I'm detailing the suspension leg hardware: an outer housing cylinder, an inner piston, a circular foot pad with segmented geometry, and a ball joint sphere at the piston base, plus figuring out where a diagonal brace rod should connect between the hull and the arm to add structural support.

I'm adding hazard striping around the cylinder housing using painted yellow-black bands instead of textures, mirroring the legs on both sides, and considering similar striping and tread detail on the foot pads, along with grille texturing for the cab's front hood plane.

Now I'm rethinking the hull and cab proportions, considering merging the hood and hull into a single extended block from the rear to the front, placing the cab on top, and adding a front bumper and grille with a possible angled nose wedge instead of a chamfer.

I'm placing side windows as glass planes on the cab, adding a roof-mounted amber light bar on a mast, and working out where roundel decals should sit on the hull sides relative to the wheel positions so they're visible above the wheels.

For the hull markings I'm positioning a star decal near the rear leg mount and a number plate reading RG-06 with a hazard label nearby. Then I'm adding fender boxes over each wheel with mud flap plates behind the rear wheels, plus rear details like a tow hitch, red glowing taillights, a ladder with rungs, and a rear plate with light boxes.

Now I'm working out the trunnion pylons that mount the gun, using angled boxes with cylindrical pins, connected by cradle side plates that run along the gun frame to support the breech block on top.

Adding the pivot pin cylinder through the trunnion, then sketching power cables as catmull sweeps from capacitors to the breech rails. I'll add a lathed radar dish on the cab roof, a sensor mast, thin antenna rods, and finish the front with glowing headlights and hazard-striped bumper boxes.

Now I'm adding tow hooks, a winch, and a brush guard up front, plus small mirror boxes on arms, and a vertical exhaust stack cylinder behind the cab. I'm checking heights so the gun barrel clears the cab roof and mast without colliding with the rail rings.

I'm placing the mast, radar, and beacon symmetrically on either side so they clear the ring radius, then setting the gun's overall length so it extends from roughly -5.1 to 7.9 along the hull, centered near x=0 with an 8° tilt. Now I'm defining a helper function that converts along-barrel, lateral, and height offsets into world coordinates using the direction and tilt vectors.

Writing box-helper function...

I'm also planning warning-label decals on the cradle sides, oriented using local x and z axes with an up vector so they lie flush against the gun housing.

For the muzzle, I'm thinking through thin glowing boxes for the energy arc between rails, plus a monospace "RG-06" text decal, all tied into an olive-and-dark-steel color palette for the overall aesthetic.

I'm sketching out the texture set: a star roundel, a yellow hazard label with bolt icon, a stenciled "RG-06" number, glass, grille, hub, and maybe tally stripes on the barrel as kill marks. Now I'm getting ready to write this all out as compact but reasonably detailed code.

Writing armor paint shader...

Defining materials and textures...

Still working out ring spacing and placement...

Adding small lateral fins along the rails using transformed box geometry, positioning them to clear the ring side bars, and building a helper that composes each piece's position and orientation into the gun's coordinate frame.

I'm fixing the overlap in the cab profile outline so the extrusion points don't intersect the hull top, then working out the windshield's slope geometry by computing the vector and normal between the two roof points to position the glass panel correctly.

Now I'm placing the windshield plane with the right offset for the bevel, then adding side windows positioned symmetrically along the cab flanks and starting to position a roundel decal on the hull sides.

I'm checking hull visibility between the wheels and fenders, then sketching the bumper geometry with hazard-stripe paint, a grille plane, and glowing headlight boxes mounted near the front corners.

Now I'm adding rear details: a plate box, red taillight glows, a ladder with rungs and verticals near the rear, a hitch ball, and an exhaust stack cylinder with a cone cap positioned behind the cab.

I'm checking clearance between the gun and the stack, then placing a lathed radar dish on a mast with a non-self-intersecting profile, angled forward and up.

Now I'm adding details like an amber beacon, a roof light bar, mirror arms with boxes, and planning cable sweeps from the capacitor to finish assembling the model.

Next I'm working out the hydraulic elevation cylinder with rod and piston sections at different radii connecting the cradle to the gun point, plus adding ground contact pads for the deployed legs.

Now I'm defining the gun's pivot geometry and helper functions for placing components along the barrel's angle and offset, setting up the cradle positioning math before moving into the gun's material and glow ring details.

Working on the muzzle shroud and glow strip placement...

I'm adding tire paint mixing dusty tones with noise-based dirt streaks, and layering mud onto the lower hull armor. Now I'm finalizing the part builder structure, making sure glow effects wrap properly around parts, then returning the completed root object.
